item.title: A New Chatbot Wants to Unlock the Secrets in Tattered Ancient Greek Records
item.description: In the hope of uncovering new details about ancient life, researchers have developed a large language model that fills in the gaps in papyrus fragments.

item.title: How to Use AI With Your Privacy Intact
item.description: Your conversations with AI chatbots are both highly personal and deeply vulnerable to surveillance. Here’s how you can protect yourself.

item.title: AI, Tariffs, Rare Minerals: What to Expect From Trump’s Upcoming Summit With Xi Jinping
item.description: Washington and Beijing have grown ever more linked in the AI boom, making hardware exports and technological restrictions hefty bargaining chips in negotiations.

item.title: Got an Android Phone? Google Thinks You’ll Probably Want a Googlebook Laptop
item.description: Apple lovers have long enjoyed seamless connectivity between their iPhones and Macs. Now, Google’s bringing that experience to Android.

item.title: US and China Discuss Alerting Each Other to AI National Security Threats
item.description: Officials discussed setting up a mechanism for the two countries to notify each other of AI incidents which could threaten national security.

item.title: Meta's Muse Is Better at Surveilling Than Helping Me
item.description: The Muse app continues Meta’s trend of opting users into data collection for AI training. It also nudges you to share your bank account, email, and passport information.

item.title: It’s Donald Trump Versus MAGA on Data Centers
item.description: The president has doubled down on data centers and AI. His base is running in the opposite direction.

item.title: Forget the AI Slowdown—the Vulnerability Explosion Is Already Happening
item.description: AI labs are toying with an industry-wide pact to slow development. Meanwhile, widely available AI chatbots are already helping uncover a tidal wave of security flaws.

item.title: Mathematicians Hate AI. They Can’t Quit It
item.description: Powerful AI models have created an existential risk to the field, but researchers can’t stop relying on them because they’re too useful.
